subject: One yellow bicycle leaning against a blue plaster wall in clear midday light
prompt:
USER SUBJECT: One yellow bicycle leaning against a blue plaster wall in clear midday light
Preserve the user's requested identities, counts, setting, and layout. Add no default motifs.
VISUAL MEDIUM: oil_painting
REPRESENTATION: recognizable
APPLY THESE AUTHORED VISUAL RULES:
- [measured-silhouette-and-intervals] Arrange only the requested subjects with clear silhouettes and intentional intervals; use a small number of horizontal, vertical, or diagonal alignments to create rhythm without borrowing a known Seurat composition.
- [plane-sensitive-separated-pigment-marks] Apply separate nearby pigment hues in orderly dabs, short strokes, or patches whose direction and density follow the local plane; let them remain distinct close up and combine visually at normal viewing distance.
- [optical-light-and-colored-shadow] Keep the light direction and value structure simple; place related or contrasting hues next to one another where they describe illumination and shadow, without making every surface vibrate equally.
- [composition-mark-and-light-coherence] Let the arrangement, mark rhythm, and divided colors describe one coherent user-requested scene.

scope.description: A structured painting direction for user-specified scenes. Establish calm, carefully spaced forms and clear compositional rhythms, then build light and color from separate, orderly marks whose shape and density follow each form or plane. The marks may be small dabs, short strokes, or interwoven patches; they should remain visibly separate up close and cohere optically at normal viewing distance. Do not require dots or a park scene as the subject.
limitations: Preserve only the people, objects, setting, count, and relationships requested by the user.
Do not add a park, procession of figures, shoreline, or named Seurat motif by default.
Keep pigment marks orderly but varied with form; avoid uniform dots, arbitrary noise, and the impression of a printed screen.

rules.applies_when: The user requests a composed scene or object study in a measured painted style.
rules.instruction: Arrange only the requested subjects with clear silhouettes and intentional intervals; use a small number of horizontal, vertical, or diagonal alignments to create rhythm without borrowing a known Seurat composition.
rules.observable: Main forms remain individually readable and their spacing creates a quiet, deliberate visual rhythm.
rules.reject_when: The requested objects merge, arbitrary background figures are added, or the layout resembles a recognizable park or harbor painting.
rules.avoid: unrequested figures, default park setting, copied figure procession, and crowded layout

rules.applies_when: The scene uses divided color as a visible painting method.
rules.instruction: Apply separate nearby pigment hues in orderly dabs, short strokes, or patches whose direction and density follow the local plane; let them remain distinct close up and combine visually at normal viewing distance.
rules.observable: Pigment units are legible at close range, while the image reads as coherent color and light from a normal viewing distance.
rules.reject_when: Marks become identical dots, random speckle, smooth premixed gradients, or a mechanical halftone screen.
rules.avoid: uniform dots, arbitrary complementary pairs, blur, noise, and printed halftone

rules.applies_when: The user requests clear natural light or a luminous outdoor painting.
rules.instruction: Keep the light direction and value structure simple; place related or contrasting hues next to one another where they describe illumination and shadow, without making every surface vibrate equally.
rules.observable: Light and shadow remain readable through grouped color relationships, and the brightest chromatic activity stays focused on meaningful areas.
rules.reject_when: Color contrast overwhelms form, shadows become flat black, or complementary hues are paired without regard to local light.
rules.avoid: all-over neon vibration, black shadow fill, and indiscriminate color contrast

joint_checks.instruction: Let the arrangement, mark rhythm, and divided colors describe one coherent user-requested scene.
joint_checks.observable: Requested forms remain count-correct and readable; mark behavior follows planes; colors cohere at viewing distance without losing their separate painted character.

review.note: Successful compilation is not image-quality validation or a maturity upgrade.
